findings.title: retryCount delete clause is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: SMS` condition. It applies to every WorkflowReminder, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP ones. Any reminder of another method that later gets a retryCount above 1 would be deleted by this SMS cron. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

findings.title: Retry threshold deletes only after a third attempt, contradicting the stated behaviour
findings.body: The PR says the reminder is deleted after scheduling failed twice. With `gt: 1`, deletion happens at the start of the next cron run once retryCount is 2, which is after two failures. That matches. However, the unscheduled query does not filter on retryCount, so the reminder is not excluded until the next run's delete. Deletion therefore depends on cron ordering. This is fragile, and the query should also filter `retryCount < 2`.

findings.title: Retry update in the catch block can throw and abort the whole loop
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch is not guarded. If it fails, for example because the reminder was deleted concurrently, the exception escapes the loop. The remaining reminders are skipped and the request returns a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch.

findings.title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message never count as a retry
findings.body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing, for example an invalid or absent phone number, the code neither schedules nor increments retryCount. Those reminders are retried on every cron run until their date passes, which is the exact problem the PR aims to fix.
